To avoid this issue, we need to limit the temp file usage. PostgreSQL have the parameter temp_file_limit . Description from PostgreSQL pages pasted below [19.4. Resource Consumption](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/11/runtime-config-resource.html)  .
This is per process limit. 

We should limit this based on the size of the disk allocated. 

E.g 
Limit to 20% total disk usage.  If max_connections are set to 100 and total disk is 100G then 20G can be distributed among the 100 connections by setting the 200M as limit. We can add some buffer since not all the concurrent connections are expected to use disk simultaneously. So we can go with 400M for each.

**Test case:**

Postgres backend does not go beyond the spill limit set and backend terminates gracefully.

We plan to limit this to 40% of the disk. For many use cases this may break if 40% of disk is not available for temp files but this seems like a reasonable default.
 
**E.g --** 
Total disk == 100G , max_connections = 100
If we limit to 20% total disk usage == 20G.
20G can be distributed among the 100 connections by setting the 200M as limit.
We can add some buffer since not all the concurrent connections are expected to use disk simultaneously. So we probably can go with 400M for each ..
Currently we will switch the default to 1GB for temp_file_limit and wont implement based on the disk size.

issue.body:
### Description

`temp_file_limit` was previously set to unlimited. In 2.14 and 2.15 we have reduced the defaults to 1G to avoid the disk being filled by  rogue queries. 

We should update the documentation to reflect this change.

corresponding GH issue #12783
